newsitem.title: USA: FAA to fine Ecuador airline $285,000 over safety.
newsitem.headline: FAA to fine Ecuador airline $285,000 over safety.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration said Wednesday it proposed fining Aerolineas Nacionales del Ecuador (ANDES) $285,000 for alleged failure to stick to maximum weight requirements for operating a plane.

The FAA said in a statement its safety inspectors found that between July 17 and August 19, 1996, ANDES had operated a DC-8-53F in excess of maximum permissible zero fuel weight and maximum cargo pallet position weights.

"The FAA determined that ANDES' failure to comply with weight limitations created a particularly unsafe condition in that, as a result, weight and balance and center of gravity computations could not properly be assured," it said.
ANDES, which had been authorized to fly to and from the U.S., has 14 days to respond to a civil penalty letter issued by the FAA before the FAA takes any further action.

The FAA said Ecuador's civil aviation authority had indefinitely suspended ANDES' operating authority in October 1996 because of maintenance discrepancies involving failure to have in place internal controls or oversight of maintenance.
